newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL/EAST EUROPE - APRIL 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL/EAST EUROPE - APRIL 9.

text.p: (Contains Slovakia, Slovenia and Austria)
SLOVAKIA:

PRAVDA - Opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) deputy Mikulas Dzurinda said the the planned joint-venture between Slovakia's state-run gas distrubutor SPP and the Russian Gazprom will increase Bratislava's dependance on Russia.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Economics Ministry said it was not considering re-imposing an import surcharge, but added that prepared measures designed to help improve the trade balance could include quotas on unspecified imports.
- Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik and the EBRD are expected to negotiate the sale of the bank's stake in Slovak oil refiner Slovnaft to the government at the fortchoming annual meeting of the EBRD.
- Slovakia and Greece on Tuesday signed an air traffic agreement.

NARODNA OBRODA - Steel producer VSZ will suply steel pipes to a planned water system in Montenegro. The contract is worth some $12 million, the main contractor is Slovak construction company Hydrostav.
SME - The Slovak government demands that Czech President Vaclav Havel apologises for his recent comments on Slovakia's integration into NATO. -- Bratislava Newsroom, 421-7-521-8402
SLOVENIA:
DELO

- Slovenian Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler met his Hungarian counterpart Laszlo Kovacs on Tuesday, they discussed mutual cooperation and possibilities of the two states to join NATO in the first round of its enlargement.
- Prime Minster Janez Drnovsek on Tuesday called trade unions and employers to sign an agreement on social benefits as soon as possible.
- Costs for opening custodian accounts for international portfolio investors should be lower in order to increase compatitiveness of Slovenian banks, finance minister said on Tuesday.
- A four-day financial fair Kapital 97 was opened by Finance Minister Mitja Gaspari, on Tuesday.
- Slovenian government said it will ensure 3.2 billion tolars ($20.4 million) for science and research activities in the first half of this year.

- Paper-mill Radece said it managed to cut its 1996 losses to 127 million tolars down from 1.7 billion in 1995. Radece planned to lift this year's paper production to 38,000 tonnes from 32,000 in the previous year.
DNEVNIK
- Slovenian government is expected to decide whether to lift drug prices by 6.3 percent on Thursday.
FINANCE
- Construction company SCT on Tuesday reported its 1996 profit of 26 million tolars, breaking out of red figures for the first time after three years of lack of business. REUTER
AUSTRIA:
The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- New legal action is planned against the labour contract laws, which were introduced last year, after the constitutional court decided the charges so far were not suitable.

- Steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm will raise its dividend to 26 schillings from 25 even though pre-tax profits slacked to 1.3 billion schillings from 1.5 billion. After restructuring measures expansion is planned. A minority share in a unit of Germany's steelmaker Thyssen is also planned.
- Oil and chemicals producer OMV plans to cut more jobs even though pre-tax profits jumped to 2.92 billion schillngs from 2.19 billion. The dividend will be raised by three to 23 schillings.
- Austia's Chamber of Economy wants to save 500 million schillings by demanding fees for its assistance of export.
- The City of Vienna will subsidise innovative and technological companies with 470 million schillings this year.

- Constructor Porr, a unit of Creditanstalt, is slowly starting cooperation with contructor Universale both of which were brought together by the latter's parent Bank Austria's takeover of Creditanstalt.
- Austria's paper industry hopes for a slow improvement of the economy as sales went down ten percent in 1996.
- Papermaker Frantschach expects to be awarded the majority stake of Poland's biggest papermaker. A co-operation with Germany's Vereingte Papierfabriken is also planned.

- The European Union's ruling on transit through the Alps is expected for June at a special minister's council. Austria threatens to impose a ban on trucks driving at night on the country's main transit route.
DIE PRESSE
- The Social Democrat Party has sold its 100-million-schilling stake in Austria's central bank. It is expected that the stake was sold to Bank Austria.
- Health Minister Lore Hostasch announced the government will continue its austerity measures in the health area too as long as it does not threaten the quality of treatment for patients.
- Austria's exporters are showing too little interest in trade with Asia. While the trading deficit with Japan could successfully be reduced, trade with China can still be improved.

- Austria's state-owned Post & Telekom Austria (PTA) plans to double pofits by the year 2000 even though the market will be liberalised and telephone prices will sink by cutting up to 8,000 jobs and increasing the profitability of the company.
- A strategic partner for PTA's mobile phone unit Mobilkom should be found by the end of the month. Four international groups have shown interest so far.

- Wolfgang Ruttenstorfer, state secretary for the Finance Ministry, has repeated the government's stand that the introduction of the European Union's single currency euro will not lead to rises of prices or fees. The government will check on retailers not to raise prices.
KURIER
- First balances of Austria's budget in the first quarter show a slump in tax income.
- Conservative party leader Wolfgang Schuessel says his party is "consciously conservative" to increase the difference to the senior coalition partners.
- Austrian papermakers demand free access to a liberalised electricity market as it fears high costs in international competition.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Shareholders are protesting against a new takeover law which would make offers for small shareholders up to 25 percent lower.
- Real estate company Erste Immobilien AG will raise its capital to 1.215 million schillings by the sale of shares worth 202,5 million schillings.
